'''David Savitt''' is a Canadian-American [[mathematician]] working in algebraic number theory and arithmetic aspects of the [[Langlands program|Langlands Program]].

Savitt received the [[Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers|Presidential Early Career Award for Scientists and Engineers (PECASE)]] in 2014,<ref>{{cite news|last=Eaton|first=Elizabeth|date=January 27, 2014|title=UA math professor recognized by White House|newspaper=The Daily Wildcat|url=https://wildcat.arizona.edu/140752/news/ua-math-professor-recognized-by-white-house/}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first=Carol Ann|last=Alaimo|date=January 18, 2014|title=UA math prof wins White House award|newspaper=Arizona Daily Star|url=https://tucson.com/news/local/education/college/ua-math-prof-wins-white-house-award/article_42552d35-ed61-5de6-9ba9-f2e51e3e9dda.html}}</ref> and was named a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2017.<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society|title=2017 Class of Fellows of the AMS|url=https://www.ams.org/grants-awards/ams-fellows/rnoti-p268.pdf}}</ref>

== Career ==
Savitt earned his Bachelor's degree in 1996 from the [[University of British Columbia]]. After completing his doctorate at [[Harvard University]] in 2001 under the supervision of [[Richard Taylor (mathematician)|Richard Taylor]], he held postdoctoral fellowships at [[McGill University]] and [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques|IHÉS]] From 2005 to 2015 he served on the faculty of the [[University of Arizona]], after which he moved to [[Johns Hopkins University|Johns Hopkins]], where he has been department chair since 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Four Johns Hopkins professors to speak at the 2026 International Congress of Mathematicians|first=Rachel|last=Wallach|date= July 30, 2025|website=Johns Hopkins University|url=https://hub.jhu.edu/2025/07/30/johns-hopkins-professors-2026-international-congress-of-mathematicians/}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://math.jhu.edu/~savitt/CV.pdf|title=David Savitt CV|accessdate=2026-03-19}}</ref>

With [[Toby Gee]] and Tong Liu, he proved the weight part of [[Serre's modularity conjecture|Serre's conjecture]] for [[Hilbert modular form|Hilbert modular forms]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Gee|first1=Toby|last2=Liu|first2=Tong|last3=Savitt|first3=David|date=February 2015|title=The weight part of Serre's conjecture for GL(2)|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/forum-of-mathematics-pi/article/weight-part-of-serres-conjecture-for-textgl2/0770F04028B20A93BBFD87F33B56C141|journal=Forum of Mathematics, Pi|language=en|volume=3|doi=10.1017/fmp.2015.1|arxiv=1309.0527}}</ref> and with [[Matthew Emerton]] and [[Toby Gee]] he proved [[Christophe Breuil|Breuil]]'s conjecture on local-global compatibility for lattices in the cohomology of Shimura curves.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Emerton|first1=Matthew|last2=Gee|first2=Toby|last3=Savitt|first3=David|date=April 2014|title=Lattices in the cohomology of Shimura curves|journal=Inventiones mathematicae|volume=200|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00222-014-0517-0|arxiv=1305.1594}}</ref>

== Outreach ==
Savitt is a director of [[Canada/USA Mathcamp]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Mathcamp Board of Directors|website=mathcamp.org|url=https://www.mathcamp.org/about_mathcamp/board/}}</ref> an academic summer program for middle and high school students in mathematics, where he was also an instructor for many years.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Roberts|first=Siobhan|date=August 16, 2003|title=Strength in Numbers|url=https://siobhanroberts.com/strength-in-numbers/|newspaper=The Globe and Mail}}</ref>
